walkthroughs.body_html:
HL Extension Topics and Quantitative Analysis — a core area of Economics.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

HL Extension Topics and Quantitative Analysis brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with HL Extension Topics and Quantitative Analysis.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Alfred Marshall published 'Principles of Economics' establishing supply-demand analysis in:
A fall in the price of a substitute good causes demand to:
options: Decrease (curve shifts left)
Increase (shifts right)
Stay constant
Become vertical

mcqs.q: What does price elasticity of demand measure?
options: The responsiveness of quantity demanded to a change in price — the percentage change in quantity divided by the percentage change in price.
CPI measures consumer prices and RPI measures retail prices — that's the only difference.
PED measures how flexible or stretchy a product is.
PED measures whether a product is expensive or cheap.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between CPI and RPI as inflation measures?
options: Both measure price changes via a basket of goods, but RPI includes housing costs (mortgage interest) and uses an arithmetic mean; CPI excludes housing costs and uses a geometric mean — CPI is the official UK target measure.
CPI and RPI always give the same inflation figure.
PED measures whether a product is expensive or cheap.
CPI measures consumer prices and RPI measures retail prices — that's the only difference.
Automatic stabilisers are special government emergency funds.

Features of the tax and benefit system that automatically cushion the economy without new legislation — e.g. unemployment benefits rise in slumps; tax revenues fall as incomes fall, supporting demand.
PED measures whether a product is expensive or cheap.
Automatic stabilisers are interest rate changes by the central bank.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Consumer surplus”?
options: Quantity producers willing and able to sell at each price; usually positively sloped.
Price change moves along curve; non-price determinants shift curve entirely.
Alfred Marshall's demand-supply diagram in 'Principles of Economics' 1890.
Area below demand curve above price; willingness to pay minus actual price.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Shifts vs movements”?
options: Quantity of good consumers are willing and able to buy at each price, ceteris paribus; inverse relation to price.
Quantity producers willing and able to sell at each price; usually positively sloped.
Price where Qd = Qs; market clears with no shortage or surplus.
Price change moves along curve; non-price determinants shift curve entirely.
